change: Extract from the Saudi Exchange XBRL renderings first, then locate every figure in the PDF for a page reference.
reason: The archive holds an XBRL .xls for nearly every filing, with entity, period, currency and rounding embedded, which makes company/period/unit verification mechanical. PDFs remain the primary document for page references and notes.

change: Choose the 'latest restated' value by the period a document covers, not by its filing date.
reason: ANB re-filed several 2022–2023 XBRL files in 2025; ordering by filing date would have picked a re-filed old interim over the next annual report.

change: Cross-check every value across all documents that present it and flag differences above 0.5% as restatement or unit error.
reason: Found a unit-declaration error (Petro Rabigh Q2 2023 XBRL declared 'Actuals' for thousands) and real restatements (Petro Rabigh FY2024 revenue; FY2024 bank equity restated in 9M 2025 interims).

change: Classify bank income-statement lines by position (above 'Total operating income' / inside 'Total operating expenses') rather than by label alone.
reason: Fee lines switch between net and gross+expense presentations, impairments sit inside operating expenses, and some 'other operating expenses' are deductions within operating income.

change: Keep an overrides register for XBRL gaps and mis-tags, each with PDF page and reason.
reason: ADES 9M 2026 has no XBRL; ANB FY2024 XBRL is unreadable; Al Rajhi's FY2022 comparative in the FY2023 XBRL tags FX income as a fee line.

change: Re-save malformed .xls files through LibreOffice before declaring them unreadable.
reason: 11 bank annual XBRL files failed the standard reader; 10 were recovered this way.

change: Flag scanned PDFs (no text layer) in the source register and verify their figures visually.
reason: 73 PDFs in the two pilot sectors have no extractable text on the first pages (e.g. Bahri primary statements, many bank interims).

change: Calculate operating income consistently for 'nature of expense' income statements (PBT + finance costs − finance income − share of associates) and label it C.
reason: Aramco and SARCO do not present an operating-profit line; without this, sector operating income and EBITDA would mix definitions.

change: Show company-specific top-line items (e.g. Aramco's other income related to sales) separately and keep them out of the sector top line.
reason: Keeps sector revenue on one IFRS definition while preserving Aramco's own presentation.

change: Treat growth on a zero or negative base as 'n.m.' everywhere, including sector totals excluding the largest company.
reason: Energy excluding Aramco is loss-making in FY2023–FY2025, so percentage growth is meaningless there; absolute changes are shown instead.

change: Use interim-report management pages for operating KPIs where annual PDFs carry only financial statements.
reason: Aramco's interim reports include realised price and production, which allow a price/volume split for 9M; the annual files in the archive do not.

change: Take sector membership from the Saudi Exchange's current classification (checked against the archive folder and manifest sector field) and apply it to every period.
reason: Aldrees (4200) was reclassified from Energy to Consumer Discretionary on 14 Sep 2025 and Luberef (2223) is in Materials; a constant universe keeps growth rates comparable and the move is stated in the sector note.

change: Exclude archive files whose names mark them STALE / DO-NOT-USE or UNKNOWN-PERIOD, and log the exclusion.
reason: Present in Capital Goods, Consumer Services, Food & Beverages, Health Care, Insurance and Materials folders (not in the two pilots).

change: Separate 'investment holding' companies with no revenue (e.g. SARCO) from revenue-based ratios and growth.
reason: SARCO reports no revenue; revenue-based margins are not meaningful and it is shown on a profit basis only.

change: For banks, build ROE on ordinary equity (excluding Tier 1 sukuk, after Tier 1 distributions) and keep bank-reported ROE as reference only.
reason: Tier 1 sukuk are classified in equity and their size differs widely between banks; reported ROE definitions differ.

change: Apply a SAR 10m materiality floor: growth, CAGR and revenue-based margins on a smaller base are n.m., in Python and in the workbook formulas alike.
reason: SARCO's 9M 2026 margins (−2,221%) and capex growth (+7,288%) were arithmetically correct but meaningless; one shared constant (calc.MIN_BASE) keeps the HTML and the workbook in step.

change: Run check_narratives.py in every build: unresolved reference chips fail the build, and ratio levels quoted in company text are compared with the calculated ratios.
reason: The HTML review found 8 chips that opened 'not found' and Aramco text quoting margins on a different base from the table below it.

change: Write narrative margins on the same base as the ratio table (state the base once), and label every period in concentration statements.
reason: Readers compare the text with the table directly underneath; mixed bases (IFRS revenue vs margin base) and mixed periods (FY2025 vs 9M 2026 shares) read as errors.

change: Embed supporting facts (inputs to calculated figures, referenced lines such as commission expense or zakat) so every calculated figure shows its formula with clickable inputs.
reason: Calculated figures were hard to audit from the drawer; the inputs already existed in facts.csv.

change: Detect scanned statements from the statement pages themselves (title in the page heading, at least 10 amounts), not from image-only cover or auditor pages.
reason: The page-count heuristic mislabelled ADES FY2022 and three bank annual reports as scanned, and the first fix wrongly cleared Riyad Bank's image-only interims.

change: Make the HTML output phone-first: charts drawn at card width, a full-year / 9M switch for period tables, stacked cards for text tables, scope and comparison held in the URL.
reason: On a 390 px phone the original page showed 7 px chart text and hid the 9M columns two swipes away.

change: Recalculate the workbook as a required build step and verify cached values before delivery.
reason: A rebuild without recalculation delivered a workbook whose formulas read as empty in non-Excel readers.

change: Banks: compute cost of risk from the ECL charge on loans and financing in each bank's credit-risk note (net of recoveries), over average net loans, in basis points; label any residual basis difference per bank-period.
reason: The income-statement credit-loss line mixes loans, investments, due-from-banks and commitments differently by bank (e.g. Alinma FY2025: SAR 1.0bn vs 1.9bn on loans), which changed the sector trend.

change: Trace every figure, not a sample: text search, OCR of every image-only page (retrying sideways pages rotated), a check that each match sits on a line naming the item, and a hand check of everything unlocated or unclear plus a random sample of automatic matches.
reason: The sample reviews covered about one value in five; the full trace found 14 wrong values the samples had missed.

change: EBITDA add-backs: include right-of-use depreciation and impairments/remeasurements of non-financial assets (incl. held for sale); exclude receivable ECL and provisions; check the XBRL add-back rows against the printed cash-flow statement.
reason: XBRL add-back rows omitted right-of-use depreciation (Bahri, SARCO) and mixed receivable provisions and disposal gains into impairments (Arabian Drilling).

change: Give every one-off a tax and minority-share status; adjust net profit only where the filing discloses both, and never subtract a pre-tax gain from net profit.
reason: Underlying profit was not determinable for 24 of 25 material items; a precise adjusted figure would have been unsupported.

change: Check interim operating cash flow and other XBRL subtotals against the printed statement total (and its tie to the change in cash).
reason: SNB's 9M XBRL cash flows had a sign error and SAIB's omitted a new line.
